transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
Ahead of the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the U.S., China, and
Russia, President Trump met one-on-one with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese
leader Xi Jinping, with Trump saying China could help end the war in Ukraine.
We're looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine, would like
to see it ended.
I think I can speak for both of us.
Ukraine is believed to be on the agenda when the three leaders hold that trilateral meeting.
Ukrainian forces hit the Crimean bridge again less than two days after a strike collapsed
an entire section of the bridge linking the Crimean Peninsula to Russia.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports that analysts say that attack may have been time to humiliate
Russian President Vladimir Putin, just as he met with President Trump and Xi Jinping.
There is no assessment of the damage of last night's strike, but the attack two days ago
sent a whole section of the bridge crashing into the sea.
Ukraine says it was a carefully planned seven-phase operation, which was carried out over multiple
weeks, and first included the weakening of Russian air defenses around one of its most
heavily guarded infrastructure sites.
It means a lot for Ukraine, because for Putin, the Korean bridge is also known as a huge
symbol of his propaganda.
That's Ukrainian parliament member Oluksandr Merezhko.
He says the successful bridge attack is a humiliation for Putin on the world stage and
has boosted Ukrainians' morale as they come under relentless Russian drone and missile
attack ahead of their fifth winter at war.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News Cave.
Democratic New York Democratic Congressman Hakeem Jeffries is on track to make history
as the nation's first black house speaker.
House Democrats overwhelmingly nominated Jeffries during a closed-door meeting Wednesday, voting
251 to 11.
With a no vote coming from a group of progressive newcomers, a full House will vote on Jeffries'
nomination with a new Congress convenience in January.
The White House has withdrawn its nominee to lead the Putin Drug Administration.
That means the agency will continue without a confirmed commissioner.
Here's NPR's Sydney Lumpkin.
A Senate health committee was supposed to vote on Dr. Heidi Overton.
Instead, Senator Bill Cassidy, who chairs the committee and is a Republican from Louisiana,
had this to say when the committee met.
The White House abandoned a viable confirmation path for Dr. Heidi Overton for FDA, saying
that she didn't have the votes to pass, which was pretty odd since there were productive
conversations taking place, and I think she would have had the votes to pass out a committee
and to pass the full Senate.
He said it's now unlikely the Republican-controlled Senate will get a chance to confirm the next
FDA commissioner before the end of the year, when they lose the majority.
After that, the next nominee's confirmation will be in the hands of a Senate controlled
by Democrats.
Sydney Lumpkin, NPR News.
This is NPR News.
In Texas, outgoing Attorney General Ken Paxton is seeking a court order to force the Houston
Police Department to cooperate with federal immigration agents, from Houston Public Media
Dominic Anthony Walsh reports.
Three days after the midterm elections, Houston Mayor John Whitmire directed police officers
to stop contacting ICE about immigration warrants, except when arresting someone on a jailable
offense.
ICE needs to be put under more stringent control, but I have no control over that.
He says he took action because Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson, a Democrat, is expected to
not enforce a state law requiring local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Paxton is asking a Fort Bend County District Court to block the policy change.
But Whitmire says the city can run out the clock until Paxton leaves office in January.
I'm Dominic Anthony Walsh in Houston.
Major League Baseball seems on track for a lockout during an owners meeting in New York
Wednesday.
MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred said owners will not budge on a salary cap.
There's one thing that I will not compromise, and that's the issue that we're hearing from
the vast majority of our fans.
They want a salary cap in floor, and on that, we will not compromise.
Players say they will never accept a salary cap, leaving both sides looking at a potential
lockout beginning in early December.
1994 marked the last time management proposed a cap that led to a seven-and-a-half-month
strike that caused the cancellation of the World Series for the first time in 90 years.
I'm Jyle Snyder, this is NPR News.
